source: Azoulay, Graff Zivin, Fons-Rosen (2019) Does science advance one funeral at a time?
finding: Quantitative test of a classic historical-philosophical claim (Planck's principle). After 452 eminent life scientists died early, collaborators' output fell, but non-collaborators' output in the subfield rose.
numbers: 452 deceased stars, 3,076 subfields; non-collaborator articles +8.6% on average; extra papers more likely highly cited; most come from outsiders.
limits: Life sciences only; the authors say the welfare effect is ambiguous; gatekeeping can help young fields.
agent_relevance: A broad claim from famous cases can be tested on thousands of units. Rule: a method claim from a few cases is a hypothesis until a larger sample is checked.

source: Azoulay et al. (2019), prior tests of Planck's principle
finding: The paper reports that the claim that established scientists accept paradigm shifts slower than novices has had little empirical support wherever tested (Hull 1978; Gorham 1991; Levin 1995).
numbers: Three prior studies cited as finding little support.
quote: received little empirical support whenever it has been put to the test
limits: Authors note paradigm shifts are rare, so such tests have low power.
agent_relevance: Even a famous, narratively appealing case-based thesis can fail when tested: weight stories below tests.

source: Wikipedia: Planck's principle (summary of Hull, Tessner, Diamond 1978; Diamond 1980; Messeri 1988)
finding: Hull et al. found age a minor factor in accepting Darwin; Diamond found age weak for accepting cliometrics; Messeri found OLDER geologists adopted plate tectonics sooner, contradicting the principle.
numbers: No sample sizes given on the page.
limits: Secondary source; original Hull 1978 paper (Science 202:717) not opened (paywalled).
agent_relevance: Tests on different episodes can reverse the direction: a single case cannot fix a rule.

source: Hull, Tessner, Diamond (1978) Planck's principle
finding: Tested whether younger scientists accepted Darwin's theory faster; reported age as a weak predictor (known only via secondary summaries; page blocked).
numbers: not read
limits: Not opened; do not cite figures.
agent_relevance: Example of turning a methodology thesis into a statistical test on one historical episode.

source: Holton (1978) / Franklin on Millikan's oil-drop data, via Wikipedia
finding: Holton said Millikan recorded more drops in his journal than he published. Franklin said the exclusions changed the value little but cut the error. Goodstein read the notebooks and said only drops with complete observations were kept.
numbers: Claimed precision 0.5%; with all data, standard error within about 2%; value 1.5924(17)e-19 C, about 0.6% from today's value.
limits: Wikipedia summary; counts of drops not given there. Three historians disagree.
agent_relevance: A famous case used in method debates is itself contested. Treat any case account as one reading and ask what the primary record shows.

source: Wikipedia: Gregor Mendel, Fisher 1936 critique and replies
finding: Fisher found Mendel's ratios too close to 3:1 and suspected falsification. Hartl and Fairbanks (2007) and Franklin et al. (2008) argued the charge is unsupported. Porteous (2004) still found them implausible. Fairbanks and Schaalje found a tetrad-pollen model does not explain it.
numbers: About 28,000 plants, 1856-1863; no chi-square values on the page.
quote: the data of most, if not all, of the experiments have been falsified to agree closely with Mendel's expectations
limits: Part of the page unread; dispute unresolved.
agent_relevance: A statistical test of a historical case can itself be revised over 70 years. Keep case-derived conclusions open to revision.

source: Schickore (SEP) Scientific Discovery
finding: Hanson's Kepler reconstruction is widely agreed not to be historically adequate. Darden's mechanism method is a synthesis of several rational reconstructions and is called weakly normative. Nickles ties justification to reconstructing the discovery path.
quote: Hanson's reconstruction of the episode is not a historically adequate account of Kepler's discovery
limits: About 4% of the entry unread; no counts of cases.
agent_relevance: A reconstruction used to support a method can be bad history. Check historical adequacy before taking an operator from a case.

source: Hepburn and Andersen (SEP) Scientific Method
finding: Historicism holds methodology should fit practice. Published papers are retrospective reconstructions, so they poorly record how work was done. Bacon's method is hard to find in actual practice. The entry does not discuss selection of cases.
quote: published papers are retrospective reconstructions of these activities
limits: Does not cover selection bias in case choice directly.
agent_relevance: Our sources are reconstructions. Weight notebooks and process data over polished write-ups.

source: Laudan, Donovan, Laudan et al. (1986) Scientific change: philosophical models and historical research; (1988) Testing theories of scientific change
finding: Programme to test theories of method against many episodes with stated hypotheses, instead of single illustrations. Not opened (paywalled redirect); description from background knowledge only.
numbers: not read
limits: Do not cite details from this entry.
agent_relevance: Basis for requiring many cases and pre-stated tests, not illustrations.

source: Burian (2001) The dilemma of case studies resolved
finding: Addresses the dilemma that cases chosen to fit a theory prove little, while detached cases lack detail. Not opened (HTTP 403).
numbers: not read
limits: Do not cite details.
agent_relevance: Pointer for the selection-bias problem.

source: Kinzel (2015) Narrative and evidence
finding: Asks how narrative case studies from history of science can support claims in philosophy of science. Not opened (HTTP 403).
numbers: not read
limits: Do not cite details.
agent_relevance: Pointer for narrative-as-evidence.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas?
finding: Blind human study. LLM ideas judged more novel than expert human ideas, with feasibility not better. Reviewer agreement was low, so rating of ideas is noisy.
numbers: 49 human ideas, 49 AI, 49 AI+human rerank; 79 reviewers, 298 reviews; novelty 4.84 human vs 5.64 AI vs 5.81 rerank (p<0.01, Welch, Bonferroni); reviewer agreement 56.1% vs 66.0% at NeurIPS 2021.
limits: Ideas not executed; 7 NLP topics only.
agent_relevance: Novelty gains can come without validity. Judge ideas by executed checks (G2, G3), not rated novelty.

source: Si et al. (2024) diversity and judge quality
finding: LLM idea generation saturates: 4,000 seed ideas gave only about 200 non-duplicates. Overall score tracked novelty and excitement, not feasibility. LLM judges were weak (best reported accuracy 71.4%).
numbers: 4000 -> ~200 non-duplicate (about 5%); overall score r=0.725 with novelty, r<0.1 with feasibility.
limits: Single task type.
agent_relevance: Sampling more from one model does not give independent cases (G4).

source: Yang et al. (2024) MOOSE-Chem
finding: Rediscovery of hypotheses from recent chemistry papers. The model retrieves the right 'inspiration' papers at a high rate. Date control (model cutoff before the papers) is the claimed contamination defence.
numbers: 51 papers; hit ratio 83.7% at top 4% with GPT-4o; Llama-3.1-8B 43.5% at top 4% vs 83.0% for 70B; top 0.8%: 60.8% GPT-4o.
limits: Matching judged by GPT-4o; only 51 papers; no external replication seen.
agent_relevance: A rediscovery benchmark acts as a post-hoc case test. Cutoff dating is needed or the case is memorised.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) LLM-SRBench
finding: Famous equations (Feynman set) are recited from memory by LLMs. Transforming them or using synthetic problems lowers scores sharply.
numbers: 239 problems; best system 31.5% symbolic accuracy on LSR-Transform and 28.1% on LSR-Synth.
limits: Symbolic accuracy judged partly by LLM.
agent_relevance: Famous historical cases are contaminated; test the agent on transformed or unseen versions.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) LLM-SRBench: memorisation evidence
finding: On Feynman problems numeric error drops suddenly in the first iterations and symbolic error is low, read as memorised solutions rather than search.
numbers: Feynman benchmark has 100 physics equations.
quote: indicate memorized solutions rather than a meaningful search towards discovery
limits: Inference from curves, not a training-data audit.
agent_relevance: Treat a fast correct answer on a famous case as recall, not reasoning.

source: Chen et al. (2025) ScienceAgentBench
finding: Tasks built from published studies; agents are far from solving them even with strong models.
numbers: 102 tasks from 44 papers; best agent 32.4% unaided, 34.3% with expert knowledge; o1-preview with self-debug 42.2%.
limits: Data-driven coding tasks; contamination mitigated with two strategies.
agent_relevance: Cases from real papers give hard, checkable tests.

source: Jansen et al. (2024) DiscoveryWorld
finding: Simulated discovery tasks; humans do far better than baseline agents.
numbers: 120 tasks, 8 topics, 3 difficulty levels; 11 human scientists completed 66% of tasks on average, 55% of knowledge; best agent completed 38% easy and 18% challenge tasks; best knowledge agent 34% easy, 8% challenge.
limits: Humans played one seed with a 1 hour limit; simulation, not real history.
agent_relevance: Simulated cases avoid contamination; use them to test operators.

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) AI co-scientist
finding: System independently proposed a top-ranked hypothesis that matched an unpublished, co-timed discovery on cf-PICIs and phage tails, in two days.
numbers: One case; Elo averaged across 203 research goals.
limits: Single case; Elo is auto-evaluated; prior literature may have helped.
agent_relevance: One rediscovery shows possible, not reliable. Needs many cases and base rates.

source: Luo et al. (2024) BrainBench
finding: Backward-looking prediction of neuroscience results: LLMs beat experts. A memorisation check (zlib-perplexity ratio) found no sign of memorisation.
numbers: 15 LLMs average 81.4% vs 63.4% for 171 experts; top-20% experts 66.2%.
limits: Task is choosing the real abstract version, not discovery.
agent_relevance: A measured memorisation test is how to defend a case-based benchmark.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist
finding: End-to-end papers at low cost, but with hallucinated results and tables; automated reviewer near human on AUC.
numbers: Under $15 per paper; reviewer AUC 0.65 same as humans; F1 0.57 vs 0.49.
limits: Reviewer is itself an LLM; failure modes listed by authors.
agent_relevance: Do not trust generated write-ups as evidence; check outputs.

source: Si et al. (2024) limits of the study design
finding: Ideas were not executed; authors propose a follow-up in which ideas are carried out to learn whether judged novelty predicts outcomes.
limits: Design only.
agent_relevance: Judgments before outcomes are weak proxies for case truth.

source: Yang et al. (2024) MOOSE-Chem screening moderator
finding: Retrieval hit ratio depends on the screening setup: more rounds lose recall.
numbers: Screen window 10: 98.0% after one round, 56.5% after four; window 60: 71.6% after one round.
limits: Hit ratio averaged over 51 papers.
agent_relevance: Staged selection loses recall each round; keep rounds few.

source: Wikipedia: History and philosophy of science
finding: Integrated HPS is one origin of a unified discipline, but Kuhn said merging the two would subvert both.
quote: Subversion is not, I think, too strong a term
limits: Page gives no case-study methodology or numbers.
agent_relevance: Mixing history and theory is itself disputed.

source: Azoulay et al. (2019) moderators
finding: The effect depends on barriers: outsiders only enter subfields with a less hostile landscape for foreign ideas.
numbers: Effect is for non-collaborators; collaborator output drops.
limits: Moderator evidence is correlational.
agent_relevance: Context decides whether a lesson from cases transfers.

source: Azoulay et al. (2019) design
finding: Difference-in-differences with matched control subfields; no discernible effect in the years before death.
numbers: 452 stars; 31,142 control subfields.
limits: Premature deaths only.
agent_relevance: A method for testing case lessons against controls.
